sources.title: Brute Force
sources.text:
# Brute Force

## Attack overview
Repeated guessing or reuse of credentials can create bursts of unsuccessful authentication. A successful sign-in after failures increases investigative priority but does not prove account takeover.

## Indicators
High failed-attempt counts, multiple targeted accounts, new source networks, and sign-in success after failure bursts.

## Detection
Aggregate identity events by source and account; compare with ordinary retry behavior and check distributed attempts. Validate timestamps and distinguish service misconfiguration from deliberate guessing.

## Mitigation
Use MFA, password hygiene, measured rate limits, and lockout policies that avoid easy denial of service. Review exposed accounts and preserve authentication records.

## MITRE ID
T1110

## References
- https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/

sources.text:
# OS Credential Dumping

## Attack overview
Attackers may obtain credential material from operating system components to support later access. Process access alerts require context about signed tools and administrative tasks.

## Indicators
Unexpected access to protected authentication processes, suspicious dump files, and subsequent privileged sign-ins.

## Detection
Correlate endpoint process ancestry, protection events, and credential use; verify which account material was accessible.

## Mitigation
Harden credential storage, limit local administrators, enable credential protection, and rotate confirmed exposed secrets after approved containment.

## MITRE ID
T1003

- https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/

sources.title: Valid Accounts
sources.text:
# Valid Accounts

## Attack overview
An attacker can reuse legitimate credentials to access services. Successful login records must be evaluated in behavioral and authorization context.

## Indicators
New devices, unexpected geography, changed session patterns, unfamiliar privileged actions, and impossible concurrent activity.

## Detection
Correlate MFA results, device posture, source networks, session lineage, and normal access patterns. Consider VPN and travel effects.

## Mitigation
Use phishing-resistant MFA, short-lived privileges, conditional access, credential hygiene, and reviewed session revocation.

T1078

# Remote Desktop Protocol

## Attack overview
Remote desktop sessions can provide interactive access to other machines. Legitimate support and administration must be distinguished from lateral movement.

## Indicators
New source hosts, unusual logon times, privileged sessions, and remote access across multiple endpoints.

## Detection
Correlate destination logon records, gateway events, VPN sessions, and identity telemetry. Check session ownership and authorized support tickets.

## Mitigation
Use approved gateways, MFA, network restrictions, least privilege, and centralized remote-session auditing.

sources.text:
# Indicator Removal

## Attack overview
Attackers may delete or alter artifacts to hinder reconstruction of activity. Log retention failures may produce similar gaps.

## Indicators
Unexpected log clearing, telemetry outages, missing files, and suspicious administrative actions.

## Detection
Correlate collector health, endpoint activity, retention policies, and independent network records. Verify the cause of missing evidence.

## Mitigation
Centralize immutable audit records, alert on log-clearing actions, protect collector configuration, and investigate privileged access.

## MITRE ID
T1070

## References
